newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended firm, but off high levels amid caution on a weak rand. Golds shares were boosted by a stronger bullion price which traded near resistance levels.
Together this pushed the all-share index up 51.7 points to to finish at a new all-time closing high of 7,094.2. The previous record was 7,073.09 set on October 15, 1996.

Dealers said central Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals' comments at a press conference after the Societe Generale Frankel Pollack investment conference on the removal of some foreign exchange controls for residents in the next budget seemed to weaken the rand.
The rand lost seven cents in afternoon after touching 4.4820 bid to the dollar but was last trading at 4.4490/4590.
"The market looked more positive earlier this morning but since the rand began to fall after lunch, it has gone quiet," Johan Marais, director at Societe Generale Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
Dealers said rand hedges began to kick up as the rand weakened but there had been good demand for blue chip stock during the day.
Gold shares were also in good demand as the bullion price traded near $347 an ounce.
The market was seen taking its cue from Wall Street and the rand on Wednesday.
"I think we need clarity for the reasons of the weakness. We are in bullish sentiment," a dealer said.
The industrial index was up 52.2 points at 8,368.1 and golds gained 29.9 pints to 1,448.6 points.
Grootvlei ended up 130 cents to 10.80 on news that Harmony was bidding to buy it and Consolidated Modderfontein. Cons Modder also ended up 22 cents to 212 cents.
De Beers put on 150 cents to 150 rand, Anglo shed a rand to 276.50 cents and SA Breweries climbed 200 cents to 141.50 rand.
Vaal Reefs advanced 13 rand to 331 rand, Kloof leapt 140 cents to 36.75 rand, Western Areas added 175 cents to 56.75 rand and Driefontein was 75 cents stronger at 46.40 rand.
Near-dated share futures also ended firmer on back of positive sentiment and view that market has consolidated and should be set for further gains.
The all-share contract broke through resistance at 6,500 and industrials contract also traded firmly above 8,100 resistance.
The March all-share contract was last at 6,520/28 from 6,483, the industrial contract was at 8,145/55 from 8,078 and the golds contract was at 1,016/20 from 1,008.
